summary: Speed-Y is an interactive web prototype designed to support strategic Martian mission planning around Jezero Crater and its surrounding regions. Integrating official geospatial data from NASA Mars Trek, the platform visualizes key points of interest and preconfigured mineral targets, including silica, phyllosilicates, carbonates, and sulfates, through customizable map layers. It addresses the challenge of safe extravehicular exploration by automatically calculating distances between the main habitat and surrounding objectives, enforcing a maximum reachable perimeter with real time error alerts, and verifying elevation disparities to avoid hazardous terrain. details:
Speed-Y is a functional prototype designed to visualize and evaluate strategic mineral targets and key points of interest based on gathered data. The platform integrates information directly from NASA Mars Trek through customizable map layers, focusing primarily on Jezero Crater and its surrounding regions as potential sites for future missions. Users can select preconfigured missions centered on specific minerals of interest, including silica, phyllosilicates, carbonates, and sulfates. To ensure operational feasibility, the system calculates and enforces the maximum reachable distance from a designated starting point, triggering an error message if a modified route or added objective exceeds the safe perimeter. Furthermore, operators can define the distance between the main habitat and surrounding objectives while verifying elevation disparities, a crucial feature designed to avoid overly strenuous terrain and safeguard astronaut safety.

Developed using web technologies such as HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, hosted via Google Sites, and supported by official geospatial datasets from NASA Mars Trek and Mars 2020 imagery, Speed-Y demonstrates how complex planetary data can be translated into an intuitive operational experience. Its primary benefit lies in providing a practical decision support tool that streamlines mission planning and makes it effortless to evaluate distances relative to objects and areas of interest. Ultimately, the project's greatest achievement is delivering an interactive map prototype that visualizes potential astronaut actions and destinations through the engaging, intuitive lens of a sandbox game. While conscious of the boundaries inherent to a lightweight prototype rather than a massive production, Speed-Y stands as a proud solo creation representing some of the most fascinating locations on the Martian surface.
